Axonal motor nerve injury produces chronic neurogenic denervation in affected muscles. Electrophysiology demonstrates reduced recruitment and neurogenic motor-unit changes, sometimes with active spontaneous potentials. This supplies a clinical substrate for weakness and wasting; the molecular steps from neprilysin deficiency to motor axon injury remain incompletely resolved.

The Italian 91% lower-limb and 56% upper-limb figures describe a mixed variant-classification cohort and are retained as context rather than a disease-wide band.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and genetic features of CMT2T in Italian patients confirm the importance of MME pathogenic variants in idiopathic, late-onset axonal neuropathies.
evidence.snippet: LL deep tendon reflexes (DTRs) are absent or reduced in 91% of patients, meanwhile UL DTRs are abnormal in 56%

nodes.description: Steppage is a characteristic compensatory gait in patients with weak foot dorsiflexors. It was documented in the Iranian biallelic p.Gln522* family and in the European family follow-up.

evidence.reference_title: A nonsense mutation in MME gene associates with autosomal recessive late-onset Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.
evidence.snippet: He currently shows typical symptoms of CMT including walking difficulty, bilateral foot drop, steppage gait, foot deformities (hammer toe), and loss of pain and temperature sensation in the lower parts of hands and feet.
